`chorale_report()` writes `report.html` and the machine-readable tables beside it. The HTML uses the
same values as the tables and states which controls were run, so it is the place to start.

The modalities were measured on different individuals, so what connects them is a fixed vocabulary
of named biological concepts: a concept is a set of features that belong together for a stated
biological reason, and every modality is scored on the same concepts. Every table below is organised
by concept for that reason.

## `concepts.tsv`: the primary result

One row per concept and phenotype contrast.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `concept`, `term` | The concept and the phenotype contrast the row is about. |
| `n_modalities`, `modalities` | How many modalities express the concept, and which. |
| `in_all_modalities` | Whether every modality of the collection expresses it. |
| `effect_<m>`, `z_<m>` | The adjusted case-control effect in modality `m`, in standard deviations of the concept score, and its ratio to its standard error. |
| `joint_effect`, `joint_z` | The inverse-variance combination across the modalities that express the concept. |
| `sign_agreement` | Share of those modalities whose effect points the same way as the combination. |
| `heterogeneity_p` | Cochran's Q for the modalities being one quantity. A small value means they are not. |
| `max_jaccard`, `attributed_z` | The largest overlap with another concept, and the statistic that survives once overlapping concepts are regressed out. |
| `p_value` | Permutation p-value for this concept alone. |
| `p_family` | Permutation p-value against the largest statistic anywhere in the vocabulary. |
| `q_value` | False discovery rate over the vocabulary at this threshold. |
| `significant` | Whether `q_value` clears the configured level. |
| `beats_best_single` | Whether the combination exceeds the best any one modality reached. |

Four columns decide how much a supported concept is worth, and they answer different questions.
`joint_z` says how strong the combined evidence is. `sign_agreement` says whether the modalities
agree; a large statistic with agreement of 0.5 is one modality carrying the others.
`heterogeneity_p` says whether they are consistent with one underlying effect. `attributed_z` says
whether the signal belongs to the concept or to the concepts it overlaps.

`p_family` and `q_value` control different things and neither is a correction applied to the other.
`p_family` is the probability of any false call anywhere in the vocabulary; `q_value` is the share
of calls expected to be false at that threshold. Both come from the same permutations, so both carry
the dependence that overlapping concepts have rather than assuming it away.

## `concept_effects.tsv`: one row per concept per modality

The unaggregated effects: `effect`, `se` and `z` per modality, with `n_features`, the number of
features that modality has for the concept, and the same overlap columns computed within that
modality. Read `n_features` before reading an effect. A concept a modality reaches through five
features is a different measurement from one it reaches through five hundred.

## `concept_coverage.tsv`: what could be tested at all

One row per concept per modality, carrying `n_features` and whether the modality expresses the
concept at the configured threshold. This is the table that separates two situations a bare absence
of results confuses: a collection carrying no shared signal, and a collection whose vocabulary
reaches too little of the measured features to ask the question.

## `variance.tsv` and `concept_variance.tsv`: what each channel holds

`variance.tsv` gives, per modality, the share of variance the concept scores reconstruct, the share
the free dimensions carry, and the share left over. The three partition the variance of the analysis
matrix. Most of the total is feature-level noise in any bulk assay, so the interesting comparison is
between the first two rather than against one.

`max_free_concept_correlation` is a check on the construction rather than a result. The projection
is onto the space the concept scores span, so the residual is orthogonal to every concept score and
the value is zero to numerical precision. A value that is not near zero would mean the two channels
are reporting the same signal twice.

`concept_variance.tsv` gives the share each concept carries on its own, in each modality.

## `free_dimensions.tsv`: what the vocabulary cannot name

A fixed vocabulary bounds what the concept channel can express. Coordinated variation outside it is
carried here.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `modality`, `dimension` | Which free dimension the row is about. |
| `variance_share` | Share of the modality's variance this dimension reconstructs. The dimensions of a modality sum to the free share the channel carries; where they cannot, no per-dimension share is reported. |
| `reproducibility` | Mean matched correlation with the same dimension recovered from other initialisations. |
| `effect`, `se`, `z` | The adjusted case-control effect on the dimension. |
| `p_value`, `p_family` | Calibrated against the same permuted phenotypes as the concepts, with `p_family` taken against the largest statistic over every free dimension. |
| `outside_vocabulary` | Whether the dimension is called at the configured level. |
| `top_features` | The features loading on it most heavily. |

`top_features` describes a dimension; it does not identify it. A free dimension has no name, and
naming it from its loadings is the reader's inference rather than the method's output.

The concept channel is fitted first, so the free dimensions hold only what is orthogonal to every
concept score. A phenotype-linked direction that shares its direction with a concept is carried by
that concept and does not appear here.

## `added_value.tsv`: whether integration was needed

`joint_z` beside `best_single_z`, their difference as `margin`, and `needs_multiple`. A concept only
one modality expresses cannot need more than one modality, whatever its statistic, and is marked
accordingly. A positive margin is what separates a result integration produced from a result one
modality produced and the others accompanied.

## `controls.tsv`: what would have caught an artefact

One row per control, with the smallest p-value that control can attain beside its result.

| Control | What it breaks | When it is inapplicable |
|---|---|---|
| Phenotype permutation | The part of the score the adjusting covariates do not explain, with the design held fixed | Never; it is the calibration the reported p-values come from. |
| Modality shuffle | The assignment of samples to modalities, after pooling | Always, as a test. It is reported as a description. |
| Initialisation stability | Nothing; it reports how reproducibly the free dimensions were recovered | Where no free dimensions were fitted. |

The modality shuffle carries a median statistic and no p-value. Pooling keeps only the features the
modalities share, so the shuffled collections are scored on a smaller feature space and often on a
smaller vocabulary than the fit; the reallocation preserves neither each modality's sample count nor
its phenotype and covariate composition; and the statistic it would be read against was computed on
the full assays. The median across shuffles describes how much of the result survives that
treatment, and nothing about it is an error rate. An inferential form needs the observed statistic
refitted on the common features alone, feature spaces that can be pooled, and modality labels
permuted within declared design cells with each modality keeping its count in every cell.

A control that could not be computed is named with its reason rather than passed over. Reading
`smallest_attainable_p` before quoting a p-value is what stops a control being read against a
threshold it could never reach.

## `concept_scores_<m>.tsv` and `free_scores_<m>.tsv`

One row per sample, one column per concept or free dimension. These are the quantities every table
above is computed from, so they are what a downstream analysis of the same collection starts from.

## What a supported concept establishes

A coordinated case-control shift in a named piece of biology, seen in the modalities that express
the concept, at a stated error rate. Ordering cause and consequence requires timing, mediation or
perturbation. Attribution to the concept rather than to its neighbourhood is what `attributed_z`
reports, and a concept whose statistic collapses there describes the region of the vocabulary it
sits in.
